core.title: Bind a browser spec to every human-facing train
core.given: A human-facing train (one whose declared participants include a human) is declared in a plan artifact.
core.when: The tester writes or reviews browser coverage for declared trains.
core.then: Ensure at least one e2e test (browser spec) is bound to that train by the stack's train-binding syntax.
prefer: Add a dedicated e2e test for the train, bound to it by the binding header, then make it prove the train, not merely name it.
Claim: read the declared train/journey behavior; identify the user-observable outcome it should deliver.
Stimulus: enter through the declared user-facing entrypoint; perform the real browser interactions that exercise the train.
Witness: assert the final user-visible business outcome, not only navigation, a success response, or an internal state token.
avoid: Adding the binding header solely for coverage credit.
Calling an internal handler instead of walking the assembled journey.
Asserting only that the page loaded while the train behavior stays unobserved.
Counting a unit test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string as an e2e test.
Treating structural coverage as proof: a spec that only binds the train, navigates successfully, or mentions its identifier can pass coverage while the journey behavior stays unproven.
unless: Trains in which no person takes part (only wagons and systems) have no screen to drive and are out of scope.
core.why: A train with no e2e test is a silent gap: its journey can regress with nothing turning red. The binding is only the coverage handle, not the proof — binding, navigating, or naming the train satisfies coverage yet leaves behavior unproven.
evidence: Every train declared in a plan artifact with a human participant has at least one e2e test bound to it by the train-binding header.
A meaningful bound spec starts from the declared user-facing entrypoint, performs the interactions that make the train relevant, and asserts the user-observable business outcome the journey promises.
Verify: the spec would turn red if the train's user-facing behavior regressed.
verification: A structural check parses train declarations in every plan artifact under the plan root (recursively) for a human participant and matches them against train bindings in e2e test files; it reports a human-participant train with no bound e2e test at that train's plan artifact, where the gap was declared. This needs a new observer; the concrete detector and finding ids belong to the realization.

A browser spec is a test file that qualifies by either arm of the stack's role assignment: the name arm — a file matching the e2e test name pattern AND run by the stack's test runner (a file matching the pattern but not run by the runner does not qualify by this arm) — or the recognition arm — any test file whose header comments carry any of the journey recognition markers, whatever its name or runner, so a misnamed one is still judged. The recognition arm is independently sufficient; the name arm requires both its conditions conjunctively. Recognition assigns the e2e test role only, it does not make every recognition marker a valid train binding. A unit test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string is not one.
Vendored and generated trees (the stack-wide exclusion list) are never scanned.

The binding is the coverage handle, not the proof: a spec that only binds the train, navigates successfully, or mentions its identifier can satisfy the structural check while leaving the journey behavior unproven; spec quality is judged by review, not by this check.

test file carrying a train or journey binding marker in its header comments

fires: A train with a human participant is added or changed in a plan artifact and no e2e test carries a binding to its train id.
The only file mentioning the train is a unit test that holds the journey URN in a string.
An e2e test bound to a train is deleted or its binding header is removed, leaving the train uncovered.
doesNotFire: A train whose participants are only wagons and systems (no person takes part).
Files inside vendored and generated trees (the stack-wide exclusion list).
A human-facing train already bound by at least one e2e test via the train-binding header, including a misnamed test file whose header carries a journey binding marker.

Browser-spec definition split by meaning into two arms: the name arm is the CONJUNCTION of the e2e test file kind (suffix.e2e_test) and execution by the stack's test runner (tooling.test_runner = Playwright) — a `*.e2e.ts` file not run by Playwright does not qualify by this arm; the recognition arm is role assignment from the complete recognition marker set (roles.assignment carries all four markers `// Train:`, `// Journey:`, `// URN: test:train:…`, `// URN: test:journey:…`) and is independently sufficient whatever the file's name or runner — whose `// Train:` member is also the required binding syntax (urn.binding.train); recognition assigns the role only and does not make every recognition marker a valid train binding. The misnamed-still-judged rule and the URN-in-string exclusion are neutral verification. No stack-specific residue remains, so nothing here is bunOnly.

Not bunOnly.

Any test file with a header marker from the complete recognition set is assigned the e2e test role and counts as a browser spec by the independently sufficient recognition arm; the marker set is carried by roles.assignment (whose `// Train:` member doubles as the required binding, urn.binding.train). The header-comment scanner is the needed observer.

neutralityNotes: 'train', 'journey', 'wagon' and 'system' are ATDD methodology terms, not stack terms, and are kept in the core. The concrete syntaxes — plan root, e2e test name pattern, e2e test location, train-binding header, the excluded trees, and the test runner that runs browser specs — all come from the profile. The browser-spec definition has two arms: the name arm requires BOTH the e2e test name pattern (suffix.e2e_test) AND execution by the stack's test runner (tooling.test_runner), so a file matching the pattern but not run by that runner, and carrying no recognition header, is not a browser spec; the header arm is independently sufficient and is role assignment, not a new idiom: roles.assignment carries the complete recognition marker set (`// Train:`, `// Journey:`, `// URN: test:train:…`, `// URN: test:journey:…`), which decides only whether a test file plays the e2e_test role, while the binding this rule requires is urn.binding.train; recognition never makes every marker a valid train binding. roots.plan holds the root path 'plan'; the recursive scan under it is derived in the rule, not stored in the root key. The human-participant marker is carried as an entry of the existing v3 map key idiom.plan_syntax (idiom.plan_syntax#human_participant), so no key is proposed. Only this rule's detector and finding ids remain in bunOnly; the e2e framework name reaches the core through tooling.test_runner rather than as text. Per verifier_detail[4], the structural check proves only the binding, not spec quality; that limit and the review deference stay in core verification. The journey-proving half of the rule (Claim/Stimulus/Witness) is not structurally checkable in any stack and remains agent-facing prefer/avoid/evidence.
